changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.sql: UPDATE teacher_activity SET feedback = jsonb_build_object( 'general_md', feedback_adoc, 'general_html', feedback_html, 'inline', '[]'::jsonb ) WHERE feedback_adoc IS NOT NULL OR feedback_html IS NOT NULL;

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.sql: UPDATE teacher_activity SET feedback_md = feedback ->> 'general_md', feedback_html = feedback ->> 'general_html' WHERE feedback IS NOT NULL;

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment: Markdown source columns for exercise text, course exercise instructions and article text, finishing the migration that already covers feedback (EZ-1729). The matching *_adoc columns are deliberately left in place: their content is the only copy of the source for anything authored before this, and the rendered *_html is what gets served. Dropping them needs a backfill decision first.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
Make anonymous_autoassess_template non-nullable, defaulting to the empty string.
It was nullable with no default, and the PATCH that writes it treats an absent value as "leave unchanged" — so once a template was set there was no way to unset it, and "no template" had two representations depending on whether one had ever been saved. One empty-string spelling removes both problems: absent still means unchanged, and "" clears.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
Give management notifications a schedule, a severity, an optional link and an audience.
The table already existed with a single `message` column and a full admin CRUD, but no web UI ever used it, and a message once created was shown to everyone forever until an admin deleted it by id. That is why nobody used it: announcing planned maintenance meant remembering to remove the notice afterwards.
Roles are three booleans rather than a join table. There are exactly three of them and the set does not change; a join table would be tidier in the abstract and worse at every query that actually runs. All three default true, so every row that already exists keeps its current behaviour of being shown to everyone.
visible_from / visible_until are both nullable, and null is not "unset" but "no bound" — null from means visible immediately, null until means visible until removed. That makes the existing rows correct rather than requiring a backfill.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
Keep the auto-assessment result with each teacher test submission.
The solution was stored and the grade thrown away, so the testing tab could list what a teacher had tried but not what happened when they did — and re-reading a previous attempt meant running it again to find out. The same two columns anonymous_submission already carries for the same reason.
Both nullable, unlike anonymous_submission's grade. That table is written after grading succeeds, so a grade always exists by the time there is a row; teacher_submission is written before, and deliberately: when the executor is down, the teacher still has their solution in the history and can retry it rather than retyping it. Null therefore means "not graded" — an executor failure, and every row that existed before this changeset.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
Rename article.public to article.published.
The column was written by create and update and read by nothing at all, so "public" described an intention rather than a behaviour: any signed-in user could read any article, and a draft was a draft only in the author's head. This changeset ships with the code that starts enforcing it, and the rename is the point — "published" says what the flag now decides, in the same word the API and the UI use.
"Public" was also the wrong word for the new meaning. Published means readable by anyone, including someone who has never logged in, which is more than the old name implied to anyone reading it next to exercise.public.
No backfill: a rename carries the values across, both spellings mean the same thing, and there are no rows to carry in any case. No constraint work either — the column is boolean NOT NULL with no default, and no index, foreign key or check names it, so a rename leaves nothing pointing at a name that no longer exists.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
Move uploaded files out of the database and stop pretending to know what they belong to.
The bytes lived in stored_file.data as bytea. They now live in object storage under the row id, which is also the storage key and a segment of the URL the file is served from — one identifier instead of three that could disagree. Dropping the column is the storage change; there is nothing else to it.
usage_confirmed goes because it never worked. It was set false on upload and true by five copy-pasted blocks that substring-matched file ids against rendered HTML, and then read by nothing at all: no cron, no query, no endpoint. A file that was uploaded and never used stayed forever, and a file whose image was later deleted from the text stayed marked as used, because nothing ever set it back. It described an intention, like article.public did before the changeset above it.
exercise_id and article_id go for a subtler reason, and this is the part worth understanding before adding them back. There are sixteen columns across seven tables where someone can paste an image — exercise and article versions, course exercise instructions, teacher feedback, inline comments, feedback snippets — and stored_file had columns for two of them. So a file pasted into teacher feedback had no reference at all and looked, to anything that cared, exactly like an abandoned upload. Adding a column per rich-text field is a race nobody wins. Instead nothing points anywhere and a nightly sweep looks for the id in every column it could be in, which makes all sixteen identical and needs no schema change when a seventeenth appears.
What that gives up is immediate deletion: delete an exercise and its images survive until the sweep runs. A storage delay, and nothing else.
persistent marks a file the sweep must not touch because its only reference lives somewhere unscannable — a PDF linked from an e-mail, an asset named in configuration. It does not mean "important", and the column comment in Tables.kt says so at length, because that misreading ends with everything marked persistent and nothing reaped.
type becomes mime_type, which is what it holds and has always held.
The foreign key renamed at the end has been misnamed since v3.xml: fk_stored_file_teacher has pointed at account, not teacher, ever since the teacher table was dropped. Renaming a constraint is normally not worth a migration; at zero rows it costs nothing, and the alternative is leaving a name that sends the next reader looking for a table that has not existed for years.
No backfill and no data migration anywhere in this changeset, because there are no rows: stored_file is empty locally, empty on dev — which is an anonymised copy of production that deliberately preserves this table — and the web app has never had an upload affordance, so nothing but curl could ever have created one. Every destructive change here is free exactly once, and this is that once.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
EZ-1771. article_version.title is nullable in the schema and non-null in Exposed. The table was created without the constraint in v3 (EZ-1573) and core has always written a title, so this is an omission in the original createTable rather than a decision.
No backfill: measured on dev, which is an anonymised copy of production — 2 rows, 0 null.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
EZ-1771, the other two. Both created_at columns are nullable in the schema and non-null in Exposed, and unlike the title above, **nulls exist**: measured on dev, 32 rows in student_course_access and 40 in teacher_course_access. So this needs a backfill, and a changeset that only added the constraint would fail on the first null — which means core would not start, because migrations run inside the Spring context.
Why the nulls are there and why they stop here: both tables predate this changelog (they were *renamed* into their current names in initial.xml, from student_course), so created_at never had a changeset asserting anything. All four code paths that write these rows set it explicitly — AddTeachersToCourse:96, JoinCourseByInvite:56, JoinMoodleLinkedCourseByInvite:47, moodle_students:252 — so nothing ongoing produces one.
The backfill uses the course's own created_at rather than a literal, which costs one join and is strictly better data: an access row cannot predate its course, so this is a true lower bound rather than an invented date, and it displays plausibly where the value is shown as a join date (ReadParticipantsOnCourse, courses.kt). Verified available for every null row before writing this: every one of them has both.
What this gives up, said out loud: after this, "we do not know when this access was created" is no longer representable. That is the right trade here only because the reads already cannot tell the difference — both DTOs declare createdAt as DateTime?, and Exposed hands back a null from a non-nullable column unchecked, so today's behaviour is correct by accident rather than by design. Making the data match the declaration removes the accident; the alternative, making Exposed nullable to match the data, was considered and rejected because a join date that is genuinely absent for 72 old rows is not worth propagating a nullable type through every reader.
changeSet.sql:
UPDATE student_course_access a SET created_at = c.created_at FROM course c WHERE c.id = a.course_id AND a.created_at IS NULL;
UPDATE teacher_course_access a SET created_at = c.created_at FROM course c WHERE c.id = a.course_id AND a.created_at IS NULL;

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
EZ-1777. teacher_inline_comment.type becomes the InlineCommentType enum in Exposed, so the values have to be the enum's own spelling — uppercase, like grader_type and auto_grade_status, which are the same shape: a text column read through enumerationByName. The API sent and stored lowercase, because it was free text and the client picked the spelling.
Not measured on dev, unlike 210826-1 and -2, and that is a deliberate difference rather than a shortcut: those two were deciding *whether* a backfill was needed, and the answer was in the data. Here the update is correct for every possible value, so a count would not change a character of it. In production it will touch nothing at all — teacher_inline_comment does not exist in the released schema, so on the v4.0 release the createTable in 260225-2 and this run back to back against an empty table.
The third statement is the interesting one. Anything that is neither spelling is a value no client ever sent and only the missing validation allowed, so there is nothing to preserve — but it cannot stay, because a read would then fail on InlineCommentType.valueOf. It is derived from suggested_code rather than defaulted to COMMENT, because that is precisely the rule AnnotatedCodeEditor.tsx:331 uses to pick the value in the first place, which makes it a reconstruction rather than a guess.
The first two are case-insensitive while the API is now strict — it refuses 'Comment' as readily as 'banana'. That asymmetry is deliberate: what a client may send is a decision, what is already in the column is a fact, and being forgiving about the fact costs nothing here because `lower()` cannot map two distinct values onto one.
Dry-run against data rather than against the empty table :core:test builds, since a migration only ever run against no rows has not been tested: 14 rows spanning both spellings, mixed case, an empty string and a junk value came out 8 COMMENT / 6 SUGGESTION, nothing outside the enum, and every row carrying a suggestion body ending as SUGGESTION. See doc/core/migration-dry-run.sql for the template.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
EZ-1777, and the answer 210826-3 above was one step short of. That changeset normalised teacher_inline_comment.type into an enum's two spellings; this one deletes the column, because the field was a pure function of another field in the same row.
`AnnotatedCodeEditor.tsx` computed it as `suggestedCode ? 'suggestion' : 'comment'` on every save and nothing ever read it back — not core, not the app. So 'suggestion' meant exactly `suggested_code IS NOT NULL`, restated in a second column that could disagree with the first. Validating it made the two agree; dropping it makes disagreement unrepresentable, which is the stronger of the two fixes and was option 3 on the issue.
210826-3 stays in the changelog even though it is now pointless. Deleting an applied changeset does not un-apply it — it just means the changelog no longer describes what environments actually ran, and ChangelogIntegrityTest fails on exactly that. A vestigial changeset with a comment explaining itself is the cheaper outcome.
No data is lost that is not derivable: every row's `type` was `suggested_code`'s presence spelled differently. Production has neither the column nor a row in this table — it does not exist in the released schema — so this is a dev and laptop change only.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
EZ-1780. Pending Moodle invitations belonging to courses that are no longer linked.
Unlinking a course used to null `moodle_short_name` and delete nothing, so every course ever unlinked still holds its `student_moodle_pending_access` rows and their pending group assignments. `LinkCourseMoodle` deletes them from now on, and the join endpoint refuses an invite whose course is not linked — which means that without this changeset those rows become permanently un-honourable **and** stay visible: the participants page lists them as students awaiting an invitation that can no longer be accepted. Deleting them is not tidying; it is the difference between a fixed bug and a fixed bug with a residue.
Not measured, and unlike 210826-3 that is a gap rather than a non-question: this deletes production rows and the count would tell a reader how much. `SELECT count(*) FROM student_moodle_pending_access p JOIN course c ON c.id = p.course_id WHERE c.moodle_short_name IS NULL;` is the query, runnable against the anonymised dev copy. The reason it is not here is access, not judgement — and the answer cannot change what this changeset has to do, because every row it matches is an invitation the application will refuse from this release onwards.
Recoverable in the only sense that matters: re-linking the course and letting the students sync run regenerates a pending access, with a new invite id, for everyone still in the Moodle course. What cannot come back is an invitation to someone who has since left it.
Groups first, for the reason `LinkCourseMoodle` gives at more length — the foreign key that would have forced the order was dropped in 201021-2, so the order is deliberate rather than enforced.
The third statement cleans the *other* residue of the same bug, on courses that are still linked and which the first two therefore do not touch. Before this release the join deleted a student's pending access and left their pending group rows behind, so every student who ever accepted a Moodle invitation left one row per group they were in. `DeleteCourseGroup` counts those rows by group id with no join to the access row, so its "this will affect N students" warning has been inflated by them — and on a linked course with `sync_students` off, nothing ever rebuilds the table, so it stays inflated. Matching on "no access row for this (course, moodle_username)" rather than on the course, because the orphans are defined by what they no longer point at.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.comment:
EZ-1786. Bug reports filed from the app by any signed-in user.
A separate table rather than more columns on `log_report`, and the distinction is worth stating because the two look alike from a distance. `log_report` is machinery talking: the client noticed something and said so, and nobody promised to read it. A row here is a person deliberately asking for help, which means it needs an outcome — an issue id, or a record of why there isn't one — and those are the columns `log_report` has no business growing. Conflating them would also put automated client noise into the same table that `/v2/account/export` hands to the user who asked what we hold about them.
`diagnostics` is nullable because the consent checkbox is real: the dialog offers to attach the last half hour of the reporter's own activity, and unticking it has to mean something. Null is "declined", not "empty" — an important difference when reading a report that says the page went blank and shows no console output to go with it.
The `yt_*` columns are the forwarding state machine, and it lives here rather than in memory because the interesting case is the one where YouTrack is unreachable. The row is written and committed before the call is attempted; `PENDING` means nobody has tried yet, `FAILED` plus `yt_error` is what the retry sweep looks for, and `DISABLED` records that forwarding was switched off at the time rather than that it went wrong. Without the distinction a re-enabled integration cannot tell a backlog from a graveyard.
No index on `user_id`. The endpoint counts a caller's recent rows to rate-limit them, so there is a query that would use one, but it runs once per submitted bug report against a table that grows by a handful of rows a day — the sequential scan is cheaper than the write amplification for years yet. Worth revisiting if this ever becomes the automatic client error sink, which is exactly what `log_report` already is and this deliberately is not.

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.sql: WITH duplicated AS ( SELECT DISTINCT course_exercise_id, student_id FROM ( SELECT course_exercise_id, student_id, number FROM submission GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING count(*) > 1 ) d ), renumbered AS ( SELECT s.id, row_number() OVER ( PARTITION BY s.course_exercise_id, s.student_id ORDER BY s.created_at, s.id ) AS new_number FROM submission s JOIN duplicated USING (course_exercise_id, student_id) ) UPDATE submission s SET number = r.new_number FROM renumbered r WHERE s.id = r.id AND s.number <> r.new_number;

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.sql: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_ai_feedback_submission_ok ON ai_feedback (submission_id) WHERE status = 'OK'

changeSet.author: kspar
changeSet.sql: INSERT INTO student_course_exercise (student_id, course_exercise_id, latest_submission_id, submission_count, latest_submission_at, auto_grade, teacher_grade, teacher_graded_submission_id, flagged) SELECT l.student_id, l.course_exercise_id, l.id, c.n, l.created_at, ag.grade, tg.grade, tg.submission_id, c.flagged FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (course_exercise_id, student_id) id, course_exercise_id, student_id, created_at FROM submission ORDER BY course_exercise_id, student_id, number DESC, id DESC) l JOIN (SELECT course_exercise_id, student_id, count(*) AS n, bool_or(flagged) AS flagged FROM submission GROUP BY course_exercise_id, student_id) c ON c.course_exercise_id = l.course_exercise_id AND c.student_id = l.student_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT ON (submission_id) submission_id, grade FROM autograde_activity ORDER BY submission_id, created_at DESC, id DESC) ag ON ag.submission_id = l.id LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT ON (course_exercise_id, student_id) course_exercise_id, student_id, grade, submission_id FROM teacher_activity WHERE grade IS NOT NULL ORDER BY course_exercise_id, student_id, merge_window_start DESC, id DESC) tg ON tg.course_exercise_id = l.course_exercise_id AND tg.student_id = l.student_id;
